2. Reachable-set representations

Run the installed set approximation consumers

Ready · installed consumers

These three consumers use public package targets. The rotated-diamond client checks a parallelotope enclosure. The zonotope client checks its reduced generator matrix. The ellipsoid client checks two separately reviewed outer members. Each consumer constructs and checks its own result, so compare the guarantees only after reading the input and support limits below.

Reproduce this result

Full input description and JSON

The box/parallelotope client encloses a four-vertex diamond. The zonotope client reduces center 0 with generators e1, e2, and (0.5,0.5). The ellipsoidal client checks two outer members for a square. The diamond clients request four H rows and use the axis or displayed fixed direction matrix. The zonotope requests two generators with independent coefficients in [−1,1] and no factor constraints. Each directional ellipsoid member requests one outer ellipsoid; the family is their intersection. All vertex inputs have no rays.

Open the structured chapter manifest JSON

Command

ctest --test-dir build/dev -C Release -R "^installed_public_client$" --output-on-failure
build/dev/installed-consumer/build/installed_box_approximation_client
build/dev/installed-consumer/build/installed_box_parallelotope_client
build/dev/installed-consumer/build/installed_zonotope_reduction_client
build/dev/installed-consumer/build/installed_ellipsoidal_client

Expected output

Installed box approximation client: diamond is enclosed with bounds 2 on both axes
Installed box/parallelotope client: rotated diamond bounds passed
Installed zonotope client: independently admitted axis cover passed
Installed ellipsoidal client: two reviewed outer members passed

Intermediate geometry. Both the box and rotated parallelotope use the diamond with vertices (0,2),(2,0),(0,-2),(-2,0). The axis-aligned box is [-2,2]². The rotated parallelotope uses directions (1,1) and (1,-1) with bounds 2. The zonotope cover uses generators (1.5,0) and (0,1.5). The ellipsoid client checks two separately reviewed outer members.

Support limits. These are three separate numerical consumer examples, not interchangeable representations of one exact result. The zonotope output is an outer cover. The ellipsoid result is an outer family. Each result has the assurance stated by its client. First complete the installed-consumer setup in the opening chapter. Its CTest installs the current package and builds the isolated clients with find_package(CSL CONFIG).
